candidate_review: Authored and mathematically self-reviewed by the implementation assistant; independent statistical-theory expert review remains pending.

conclusions.rationale: The growing number of summands is not controlled by fixed-j convergence. Set X_{n,j}=1{j=n} deterministically. Every fixed coordinate is eventually zero, while the maximum equals one for every n.
conclusions.repair: Require a vanishing sum of tail probabilities for each epsilon, or keep the index count fixed. A vanishing maximum individual tail probability alone need not suffice.
conclusions.counterexample: The deterministic diagonal array X_{n,j}=1{j=n} satisfies the assumptions and has P(max>1/2)=1.
